- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after spikes.
- If official supply net is strongly negative (e.g., -20+), model should not over-forecast upward trend; adjust downward bias by 5–10% relative to forecast mean.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >75), model should not continue rising; introduce mean reversion bias toward prior 5–7 day average.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model is flat or rising, force downward correction by 3–5% to avoid false bullish momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mean, check sentiment history for recent volatility; if sentiment is low, reduce forecast slope.
- If official event count is high and supply net is negative, model should under-forecast peak prices to avoid overconfidence in bullish momentum.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not assume linear trend; apply smoothing filter to avoid lagged reaction to sentiment shifts.
